documents.name: Harbor Foods v. Coastline Carriers
documents.text: Harbor Foods v. Coastline Carriers (Or. Ct. App. 2023). A food distributor agreed to defend, indemnify and hold harmless its carrier against any claim "arising out of or relating to this Agreement". When the carrier's own driver injured a pedestrian, the court held the distributor liable for the whole claim: under the Commercial Indemnity Act § 3, a one-way indemnity in those words covers the indemnified party's own negligence unless the contract excludes it. A mutual indemnity limited to each party's own breach would have left the loss with the carrier.

documents.name: Pinecrest Dairy v. Northgate Freight
documents.text: Pinecrest Dairy v. Northgate Freight (Del. Super. Ct. 2021). A liability cap of three months' fees was enforced between merchants for a late delivery. The court refused to apply the cap to the carrier's disclosure of the dairy's pricing: a liability cap does not reach a breach of confidentiality unless it says so expressly. The court followed Harbor Foods v. Coastline Carriers in reading the agreement as a whole.

documents.name: Commercial Indemnity Act § 3
documents.text: Commercial Indemnity Act § 3. An indemnity for claims "arising out of or relating to" an agreement covers the indemnified party's own negligence, unless the agreement excludes it expressly. A one-way indemnity is enforceable between merchants as written.

documents.name: Commercial Late Payment Act § 4
documents.text: Commercial Late Payment Act § 4. Interest on a late payment between businesses may not exceed one and a half percent (1.5%) per month. A contract term that sets a higher rate is void as to the excess, and the creditor recovers interest at 1.5% per month.
